name: Question 11
problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x,y)=x-y$ on the portion of the disk of radius $1$ centered at the origin, where $y\le 0.$
worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region $D:$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081614/assets/95faae88fb4909a86492e45101419fe872aeb1cc2eeabde9cf773c8f71d31fff.png)

Notice that 

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot \pi \cdot {1}^{2}=\frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

The average value of the function over a region $D$ is given by

$$
{f}_{\text{ave}}=\frac{1}{\text{Area}(D)}\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dA={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\text{ }drd\theta .
$$

In polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ the region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le 1,\,\pi \le \theta \le 2\pi }.
$$

Using the change of variables formula, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}x-y\,dA & ={∬}_{Δ}(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}{r}^{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ){\int }_{0}^{1}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,\frac{1}{3}{[{r}^{3}]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )({1}^{3}-{0}^{3})\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ]_{\pi }^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[(\operatorname{sin}⁡2\pi +\operatorname{cos}⁡2\pi )-(\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi +\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi )] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(1-(-1)) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{f}_{\text{ave}}=\frac{2}{\pi }\cdot \frac{2}{3}=\frac{4}{3\pi }.
$$

Question 11

Find the average value of the function f(x,y)=x−y on the portion of the disk of radius 1 centered at the origin, where y≤0.

b
4π

23π

Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let's sketch our region D:

Notice that

Area(D)=12⋅π⋅12=π2.

The average value of the function over a region D is given by

fave=1Area(D)∬Df(x,y)dA.

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∬Df(x,y) dA=∬Δ f(rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ)r drdθ.

In polar coordinates (r,θ), the region can be expressed as

Δ={(r,θ):0≤r≤1,π≤θ≤2π}.

Using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∬Dx−ydA=∬Δ(rcos⁡θ−rsin⁡θ)rdrdθ=∫π2π∫01r2(cos⁡θ−sin⁡θ)drdθ=∫π2π(cos⁡θ−sin⁡θ)∫01r2drdθ=∫π2π(cos⁡θ−sin⁡θ)13[r3]01dθ=13∫π2π(cos⁡θ−sin⁡θ)(13−03)dθ=13∫π2π(cos⁡θ−sin⁡θ)dθ=13[sin⁡θ+cos⁡θ]π2π=13[(sin⁡2π+cos⁡2π)−(sin⁡π+cos⁡π)]=13(1−(−1))=23.

Therefore,

fave=2π⋅23=43π.
